As a big fan of fan of turn-based strategy games similar to XCOM, I absolutely can't recommend this at all.
The entire execution of the game feels mediocre. Nothing is inspired. Nothing is polished.
There's no great idea you're missing out on if you don't play this, just mediocrity.
You play with a party of 4. Strategically, it's like an XCOM game with far fewer choices/squad members/abilities. By the middle game, there are a couple ways to break the game's difficulty curve right on your knee. If you don't abuse them, strategically, the game is still like an XCOM game with far fewer interesting moving parts.
The trailers make you think the game will be stylish - ok, it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ xcom, at least it can be cool ♥♥♥♥♥♥ xcom - but they are almost misleading in terms of style, in that the game's asthetics are extremely clunky at best. Don't be deceived, you aren't even getting cool western ♥♥♥♥♥♥ XCOM here - the game is graphically sort of sitting in an uncomfortable place in that it's both not-even-AA quality yet also completely devoid of personality. Xenonauts is more endearing.
There are actually several ways in which I feel like the features are almost falsely advertised, but not quite. The first is the complete lack of style when the trailer makes it seem stylish. Another is the game saying it has an overworld. I mean, it does, technically. But it's not at all integrated with the rest of the game. It's extremely non-interactive, the game is extremely linear, you will play the same missions in the same order, the overworld does basically nothing and could almost be replaced with a series of buttons.
Well, I was clearly disappointed, so I guess that's enough to say for now.

Hard West synthesises turn-based tactical combat with a Wild West / Lovecraftian narrative. It does it relatively well too. There are various, interconnected stories, built around a Cowboys VS Demons model and they stand up alright.
Gameplay is two-fold: obviously, there is the combat setting, with your characters in turn-based battle in a given place. These are often confined to relatively similar locales, such as mining towns or caverns, as it turns out. There are various gimmicks you can employ to get an upper hand, such as "Fanning", which is basically a burst pistol shot; or "Ricochet", which is a rather amusing skill that bounced bullets off of metal surfaces. As most reviews lament, most combat relies on "Luck", which is a set resource each character has. This is diminished each time your enemies miss you with gunshots (and it is replenished when you're hit). Considering you're often outnumbered, and AI is not that dumb, this often drained off of your Luck as everybody shoots at you. Nevertheless, you can still best you opponents via covers, hit-n-runs, or such things.
The second part is the part that constitutes the gameplay between combats. It's basically a map where you move around and make choices - these determine certain outcomes in the game's world. You can spend money to get reconnaissance to pinpoint your target in a town or just wade in, slaughter everyone and "let God decide his own" (which is neat reference to the Albigensian Crusades, considering the religious theme of the story therein). Either outcome will affect your story in its own fashion.
Hard West has become cheaper and cheaper at each sale season, so it's not a completely rip-off (even at full price,, it's alright). However, it still is a bit lackluster at certain points - it lacks a certain polish and even the implementation of in-game saves was merely a last-ditch defence against player outrage of the game's Luck mechanic and the lack of save files, which could cost an entire game session in combination.
It's not "bad", by any means. But as far as tactical-combat / role-playing games are concerned, Shadowrun series can / do offer a lot more. Hard West has its peculiarity, especially those who enjoy Lovercraftian or American Western themes.

Duck Game is great.
How great? That really depends on several factors. If I was comparing this with anything else, it would be asking if you like Super Smash Brothers. Super Smash Brothers, in my opinion is only 5/10 if you’re by yourself, but a solid 10/10 when you get a couple guys to play with. Duck Game fares similarly, being a competitive, 2D, PVP focused game with skill based platforming and reaction time. The difference is that Duck Game has the one hit kill intensity found in Samurai Gunn. The kicker is that you can’t attack if you don’t have a weapon, so the start of the match is just a rapid scrambling for firearms and panicked firing. It’s an intense, skill based shootout that I hope to be playing for the next 10 years at least.
Duck Game’s true greatness is its subtleties present in its design. At first it may seem constraining to not be able to aim in all directions like you would expect, but you eventually find that if you’re pressed up against an object your duck aims upward, still allowing you to fire. A particular gun that looks like a giant magnum recoils with each shot, letting you aim slightly higher to hit enemies, essentially you exploit a handling characteristic of the weapon into a game mechanic. The ducks can even float around on stubby wings and slide on their knees if you duck while running (ha ha), allowing you to do Matrix-like dodges against your enemies. Really great stuff, with a high skill ceiling but still easy enough to allow new players to get the drop on more experienced ones, which is the “sweet spot” I adore in competitive games. There’s a button completed dedicated to quacking (SERIOUSLY) which adds a layer of absurdity and humor to the already ridiculous setting that Duck Game takes place in.
One fear I have is the staying power of the online community. Too many indie games, have I bought on a super-sale only to see that the fan base has since moved on to other games. Duck Game is still relatively new as of 6/22/2015, so finding a game isn’t too difficult, but I really, really REALLY hope this game has longevity in the future. Like I said, 10 years please. One of the upsides this game has over Samurai Gunn is its near perfect online gameplay, which I hope keeps the game alive. I only had a couple of disconnects but the lag never really messed with me too bad. Even if the online dies out, with the local play, all it requires really is a couple of controllers and a few brewskies to have a great time. I love this game.

Fallout Shelter is not like the other Fallout branded titles. In the game we play the vault manager, or shelter, where they can survive those who managed to survive the atomic war. Our adventure begins with building several rooms and placing the first settlers in the vaults. It seems to be a simple task, but over time we will find out that not all our choices are appropriate. Each individual room has a specific function. So we have a room for electricity generation, water collection, restaurant, radio or laboratory. Everyone is also important for the shelter - in the lab we produce medications, the radio station allows us to attract nearby travelers to the shelter, and the canteen provides our residents with fixed doses of food. These spaces can also be developed. The most important room is and will always be a generator of electricity. Without it, other rooms do not work. Just as they do not work without residents. However, this is not the end of the long list of options that our game offers. We need new tenants to develop our site. But they do not fall from the sky. Well, may appear from time to time out of nowhere, but such a thing happens almost at the beginning of the game. Later residents have to "bred". Gras is getting harder and harder over time. I think it is also a type of pay to win or pay to have fun game. This game has made a good impression on me. I recommend :D

After the events of The Last Revelation, it seemed that Core wouldn't make any more Tomb Raider games until the PS2 was out. However, we all just couldn't get enough of Lara Croft and thus we got Chronicles which was blatantly thrown together and boy does it really show.
In terms of gameplay, it's more or less the same as the previous games but admittedly, I really liked that they gave you the ability to roll out forwards through a crawlspace instead of having to turn around just to get down and that's literally the one good thing I can say about this game. There are many badly designed levels such as Russia where half of the time you are going through corridors in a submarine and then there's two minutes of exploring in the open water. The last level of the game is heavily bugged which the only way to counter them is to not save at all in certain parts because it will screw you over if you load up the game there.
Story-wise. we are given four different adventures of Lara Croft through her years but the first part they bring back Larson and Pierre from the first game which doesn't make any sense at all. This even takes place before TR1 so they made a massive plothole just from that. According to the trailer, Lara infiltrates the Russian base in 1984 which is where she would be only 16. Yeah, not buying that. Her trip to Ireland takes place in 1979 with her backpack yet she doesn't actually get that until she went to Cambodia with Von Croy in 1984 so... yeah, continuity errors everywhere. That shows how badly thought out they were for the story.
Would only recommend this game if you intend to play through all the Tomb Raider games. Otherwise, not really worth the time.

I like puzzle games.  Monkey's island is one of my favorite games, I still will boot up old adventure games all the time.
You know what I won't boot up again?  Broken Age.   In Monkey's island there's a lot of fun and silly stuff the player does, In most games it's an enjoyable story,  and Broken Age has a moment or two of that.
But it's a one or two note game, that tries to make a whole symphony.
The beginning of the game you get the choice between two characters, that seem unrelated.  There's the girl who... seems to be immediately thrown into peril without ANY backstory, so much so that I thought I skipped a cutscene.  Nope, just "hey you're going to be imperiled to start the story!"  She has a mediocre world to explore.
Then there's the boy, and honestly I like the world the boy is in far more.  Only thing is, that world goes on entirely too long, and the good parts of the world wanes fast.   If the game stopped after the first act, it'd be a good recommendable game
But then in the second act, the game changes, and... it's not for the better in my opinion.  It's got an interesting story arc there, but does nothing with it, and it seems that you have to go.... listen I try not to do this, but I need to talk about spoilers.  It's a rather major spoiler, but if you want to know about the second act, it's below.
Then again the quality of a puzzle game is based on the quality of the puzzles, and the good news is most of the puzzles are simple and easy to solve.  But that's also the bad news.  They're too simple.   Put round battery in the round battery sized hole.  "Talking" usually makes things almost blatantly obvious and you have to talk to everyone at least once to get all your objects anyways.
Then there are the puzzles you don't get.  If you miss a slightly puzzle, the game won't hint or help you along.  You're stuck.  Hopefully you know what to do (because the game won't help you if you get lost, or return to it after a couple months) but even if you know where you want to go, you better hope you know to do X and Y, because if not, you're going to stand around and have to just stare and hope it comes to you.  Or go use a guide.
And yeah that will happen, 90 percent of the puzzles are "go elsewhere, get something and return to me"  Where 10 percent are "you have an item that will work but we won't even hint at it."  I know I'm annoyed at the easiness of the puzzles, but the esoteric puzzles don't even give you a hint if you're stuck.  You just either get it or you don't.
Finally the story should be mentioned.  While it's a story, it feels like it's a story written for the modern generation.  Gone is the long exposition or talking.  There's beautiful moments in games like Monkey Island, where Guybrush and Elaine will talk for almost 2 minutes without player interaction.  In Broken Age there appears to be a rush.  The game almost never spends more than 2-3 lines without expecting the player to hit a button to say something.   You constantly have to choose something to say, so there's no elongated exposition.
Everything is rushed along, and quite a few parts of the game could use a little more talking such as the beginning of the game.  The story never fully develops and now in hindsight I barely remember anything that was truly unique or I'd want to see again.  I compare this to Monkey's Island again, where Elaine and Guybrush meeting, the three pirates, Stan the boat seller, and even the insult fighting are all amazing moments I could enjoy again and again.   To me that was a better story, this well, this isn't what I was expecting when I funded the kickstarter.
It's a shame because while act one is acceptable, I can't in good conscious recommend this game to anyone.  I'd recommend Monkey's Island, Grim Fandago, maybe the King's quest games, or the most games from Telltale game instead of this game.  But Broken Age, it was an interesting Kickstarter, but not a very good game, sadly.
(Note I backed the game on kickstarter, I played the game on Ps4, as part of Playstation Plus.  I did pay for this copy)

OK - Just finished the game and here are my thoughts:
What I loved:
+ Writing, voice acting and some jokes are clever.
+ Variety of weirdly thought out characters such as a talking spoon.
+ Plot is clevery written
+ Graphics are charming and in 2D.
What I didn't like:
- There are not much of areas to explore. It felt compact.
- While the plot is clevery written, it still does not capture what made classic adventure game stories interesting. There isn't much to get interested in the two main characters (Shay and Vella). We are simply solving their life problems.
- Very simplistic point-and-click game. Clicking on an object will automatically trigger whatever the progammer wanted it to be. Sometimes the character would comment on it, sometimes will try to "activate it" and sometimes will take it. I'd prefer it if it reused the verb technique, like in Curse of Monkey Island (Look at, Use/Pickup, Talk/Eat).
- The puzzles at the end of the game were frustrating and confusing.
Verdict: It is a return to classic adventure games alright but I don't see it surpassing my favourite classics (Full Throttle, Monkey Island, Grim Fandango, Sam and Max). However, it is still a recommended game for all those who still want Adventure Games. It is better than whatever Telltale is doing with Game of Thrones, that I can tell ya.

So much of this game boils down to cheap and boring gameplay elements. The game actively goes out of its way to be boring, from the expensive ammo, to the very short ranged guns, to the slow and almost pointless skill checks making looting overly time consuming, to the slow combat animations and the massive and sudden jumps in enemy health pools making combat a real drag. This is old skool gaming, without the lessons learnt from the new.
Bizarre gameplay choices, like having the weapons have big jumps in damage dealt with each tier, mean levelling up your character feel pointless as well as confusing and frustrating as you never know what ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t skill check they're going to throw at you next. Several skills are utterly useless unless you constantly level them (all the speech checks) and ultimately add little to the gameplay.
It's so close to being a good game, but it so often shoots itself in the foot with outdated and boring gameplay elements that feel unfinished, imbalanced and rushed even now.
The writing is fun and interesting, but again they shoot themself in the foot with annoying printing animation and buggy implementation. There are supposed to be secret words in the text that you can trigger but because the other character just goes 'huh?' to virtually everything you type it is very immersion breaking and ultimately a silly feature that makes you always suspect you are being cheated out of part of the story for not wanting to gruellingly type every interesting looking word.
And that word, gruelling, ultimately describes a lot of the mechanics in this game, time sinks for time sinks sake to make an actually fairly normal length game appear long. lots of walking and clicking and walking and clicking.
The director's cut hasn't really added anything much or addressed any of these issues and the truth is everytime you have a random encounter it generally feels like a chore rather than a pleasure.
If I could I'd give it a 'meh'.

Mafia 3 is a fantastic game , But like your local trip to ikea your going to see a few flaws in it's design
Monotonous mob
MAFIA 3 borrows  a lot of its formula from the open world ubisoft titles such as ASSASSINS CREED and more notably WATCH DOGS you will scour the bustling streets of this southern state breaking into junction boxes to reveal the collectables in that area and like a desperate pervert spend forty-or-so hours collecting every playboy magazine in sight. this part of the game would seem great but in MAFIA 3 its a double edged sword on one hand it adds longevity to the world you inhabit , But on the other hand it does seem tedious after you pick up your 300th fuse which you don't actually need . Unlocking junction boxes only takes up three fuses at a time . Another gripe with this game seems to be the strange design choices which I assume will be patched in at a later date for example . You have a shed load of shops that will appear on your mini map once you start walking the streets of new Bordeaux but the problem with these places are you cant do anything with them , You have bars and pawn shops and no means to get drunk or sell items, there's cloth stores dotted around the downtown area but with no means to buy outfits there's twenty or so gas stations but your vehicle never runs out of gas. I can only assume these places will become more vibrant once we get our hands on the free post content but until then these icons seem pointless.
Shadow of new Bordeaux
A game that will be brought up a lot by other reviewers is how similar this game is to SHADOW OF MORDOR in which to take down a boss and cripple his Empire you must first weaken his rackets . These range from tailing cars, smashing objects and shooting anyone that is in a four mile radius , Again this seems like a great idea but only if its used sparingly in MAFIA 3 however it isn't once your told to take down your underboss in the region an abundance of side missions will appear on your map and it goes as followed. Go to location (A) shoot a man go to location (B) steal the cash ,now repeat steps (A) and (B) five more times then lather rinse and repeat until you unlock the real story mission.
The game of the rising fun
One thing i can say that sets MAFIA 3 apart from its competition is how much it feels like your progressing through the story, normally most games in the open world genre have the full circle effect to their story and characters . For example GTA you can demolish the gangs, take out the boss and yet you still don't control the city or its people the best way to sum up what MAFIA 3 is would be to say its SAINTS ROW 1 with racism. On the latter point if your easily offended by the use of derogatory statements and slang words then maybe stay clear of this product . MAFIA 3 isn't shy to throw the N word around every four seconds . If martin Scorsese holds the record for the most F bombs in cinema then give MAFIA 3 the prize for most N words in history
The Sound of the Sixties
Mafia 3 packs an  impressive soundtrack with classics such as the number one hit from northen band the animals ( House of the rising sun ) to some more obsure songs of the era if your in your 50s playing.  This game could give you a memorable nostalgia trip and as for the other sounds that ring through your ear drums there s an  unparalleled level of detail in this package.  radio's will get interference if you embark through the sewers ,guns will tatter through fences, explosions will rip the world apart . All of the sounds feel perfect and really straps you into an immersive experience.
The southern Story
MAFIA 3 has got one thing and thats a fantasic story shot like a documentary you may stumble across on the discovery channel, it follows the FBI and other characters such as father james as they recollect the legend which is Lincoln Clay this gives the game a some what old western feel.  Talking about an outlaw that butchered the mob and took out a criminal empire . The writers that work at studio Hanger 13 are probably the most talented group of individuals on the planet I would imagine it being pretty hard to make a racist ,bigoted, discriminatory antagonist likable but heck they nailed it. Hearing Sal the main bad guy of MAFIA 3 talk throughout your excursion is like watching Kevin spacey in House of cards each line he says and each delivery he gives feels like there's purpose to it. As for our main character take note ubisoft This is how you write a strong African American character in video games. Lincoln Clay  is both charming and vengeful, Witty and humorous and is portrayed wonderfully hitting each story beat like a bullet from a gun.
The summary
MAFIA 3 really is very close to  perfection shooting feels punchy and realistic with enemies reacting accordingly to your shots , Driving feels smooth and responsive and Lincoln controls with the same animated pazazz you may see in an uncharted title with the added bonuses being the innovative way it gets you to decide who will own the town its to soon to Write-off MAFIA 3 like a car crash . But I just wished the studio didn't take out most of the content and hide it away for future post DLC. For example car customization which was present in its predecessor is now locked away for future Content along with the ability to swap clothes at will and who knows what else has been picked away . MAFIA 3 now is a skeleton but hopefully by December we will start seeing some flesh on its bones and more people may snap up this title like an alligator in the bayou and lets just say this , destiny had nothing in it but good shooting and people liked that. so there's hope for the future.

Gridrunner Rev is the oft overlooked Llamasoft game. I sorta get why, it's not the most approachable despite being clearly designed -to be- the most approachable.
That said, it's a little hard to grasp as it exists in its own world and with its own language. Exploding suns, flowers, pretty colours yet really, it's a fairly straightforward game to play with a strong scoring mechanic. Essentially, the prettier a pattern you make on screen with your bullets, the higher you score. If nothing else, that's different, right?
If I had to pull it on anything it's that it locks the best part of the game behind an awful unlock system. You have to wade through a slow and slightly uninteresting group of stages before the high score mayhem can begin in earnest. Again, a clear attempt to draw people in but let's be realistic here, Gridrunner Rev is -for- the kind of people who really enjoy score chasing.
And y'know, when the whole screen explodes around you with the Neon effects in the background it's quite the sight to behold.
So yeah, a bit janky round the edges, attempts at accessibility that fall a little flat but a great underloved gem that given some time to gel makes for a good companion piece to Space Giraffe.

Fallout Shelter is not like the other Fallout branded titles. In the game we play the vault manager, or shelter, where they can survive those who managed to survive the atomic war. Our adventure begins with building several rooms and placing the first settlers in the vaults. It seems to be a simple task, but over time we will find out that not all our choices are appropriate. Each individual room has a specific function. So we have a room for electricity generation, water collection, restaurant, radio or laboratory. Everyone is also important for the shelter - in the lab we produce medications, the radio station allows us to attract nearby travelers to the shelter, and the canteen provides our residents with fixed doses of food. These spaces can also be developed. The most important room is and will always be a generator of electricity. Without it, other rooms do not work. Just as they do not work without residents. However, this is not the end of the long list of options that our game offers. We need new tenants to develop our site. But they do not fall from the sky. Well, may appear from time to time out of nowhere, but such a thing happens almost at the beginning of the game. Later residents have to "bred". Gras is getting harder and harder over time. I think it is also a type of pay to win or pay to have fun game. This game has made a good impression on me. I recommend :D

I am a middle aged woman with a family now, but aside from a few Atari games in the early 80's and Super Mario Bros on Nintendo in the late 80's, Tomb Raider was really the first game that inspired awe in me, in the late 90's. I played all of the games, up to The Last Revelation, before life got in the way and I haven't played any other game since, until now :) Purchasing a new PS4 game console for my 6 YO son and becoming a fan of a lowbrow/pop surreal artist who has done some videogame fanart has inspired me to come back to the world of gaming and happily immerse myself again.
Of course, I'm wanting to play many games (and have already purchased over 100 of them on sale - being an adult DOES have it's perks), but I really wanted to start where I left off, which leads me to Chronicles. I have only played for a few hours today, so I'm sure I'll want to update this review at some later date but I just wanted to give a slight review of the game from the perpective of someone with children and responsibilities and as someone who has forgotten many of the talents I garnered in the past...
First of all 2 things....
If you are person who hasn't played a game in over a decade, like me and you are attempting to turn your computer into a console by purchasing an XBox360 controller, so that you can really pick up where you left off... please understand that  controller support has it's limits. Chronicles purports to offer full controller support, but when I go into options and select "joystick" and go back into the game... All Lara does is run around in circles (can't seem to get her to stop) and pull flares! It's okay, I wanted to learn how to game with a keyboard/mouse anyway, but I really didn't want to do that on an adventure game. I just wanted to sit back, relax and enjoy the story without being so clumsy and having to try failed maneuvers over and over again. I've read that controller support is way better in some of the newer version of TR, so I can't wait to try and see.
Second, incase you've forgotten! Don't wait until the end of the level for your game to be saved! I made it all the way through level 1 and was about to walk through the Bell Temple door, when I was sent off on another side mission, via a walkthrough, when I missed a jump and lost my life. 15 years ago, this would have been just frustrating, but it would have slid off of my back... but as an adult, with children to feed, a house to keep clean and a business to run... I wanted to cry and vow to never throw away another 4 hrs of my life like that again.
The game is just as I remember it (so far) but I just wish I didn't have the "you could be doing something else" angel whispering in my ear, because that makes it so much harder to enjoy the game now. But, that's a personal fault(?) and has nothing to do with the game. I would imagine the game makers assumed that users had the time to spare. I still think the graphics are very cool and they do help me to escape a bit, but I've got to be honest, I've seen the graphics on many of the newer games I've purchased, including the newer Tomb Raider titles and I really can't wait to play them.

TL;DR: I liked it. 9.3/10. Let's get ourselves a follow-up!
In all honesty, I loved this game. If you are in any way familiar with Dischan's free visual novel, "Juniper's Knot," you'll know where I am coming from.
[IN FACT, TRY THAT ONE OUT FIRST, AS IT IS FREE AND GIVES YOU THE FEEL OF THEIR STORIES JUST LOOK IT UP ON GOOGLE OR SOMETHIN'.]
The characters all have their own personality to me, and that is sometimes hard to find when you have more than one or two characters the story focuses on. I believe that this series will have more than two crucial characters.  Sometimes they all just blob together, but, well, if you play this and see the characters, you'll know who I'm talking about.
I would like to say that the story begins with Winter Harrison, who's an apprentice of sorts to help manage chaotic worlds. She is mentored by a certain Cyrus Addington - whom I absolutely adore, though that is beyond the point - and the two are sent to a certain world that is about to go over the boiling point.
The music. The music fit in so well with the story, and I never really got pulled out of my reading to think, 'Hey, this music really doesn't fit in at all.' The atmospheric sounds brought me to believe this world actually existed, and I particularly love a certain song that plays in a certain place (WOW GURL Y U NO SPOIL).
The twist in this episode really got to me. I didn't expect it at all, and I love that in a story. Too many times am I reading and I completely called the big climax, but this one had me floored. Granted, I may have just been tired and woozy from something. But I think that it was well played out by Dischan. It made me feel something; I almost gave in. When I was done, I sat there just revelling in what had happened, then jumped back in to see if I could change it. Because this episode has a crucial choice that you have to make, and you are able to save multiple stories where your decision can impact how the characters look at you and how your character looks at herself.
I have played games where your decisions don't matter at all, and you get the same speech from the same people over and over and over as you try to find some variety. This one is almost completely written differently. It may be because the choice I'm speaking of is rather drastic, but I felt as though the developers did well in almost completely rewriting how everything turns out. Winter will actuall respond to your choice. It can and will have dire consequences.
I am writing this review because I believe that not enough people know this game even exists. I just found it randomly on Steam, for a really low price. That may be my only complaint here: the price. Dischan has ceased development on the sequel to save their money, as they really didn't have much to begin with since this story was rather glossed over by some. Hopefully, this review may bring more people to enjoy the story and coax the developers back onto their feet so they can give us the next chapter in this story.

Duck Game is great.
How great? That really depends on several factors. If I was comparing this with anything else, it would be asking if you like Super Smash Brothers. Super Smash Brothers, in my opinion is only 5/10 if you’re by yourself, but a solid 10/10 when you get a couple guys to play with. Duck Game fares similarly, being a competitive, 2D, PVP focused game with skill based platforming and reaction time. The difference is that Duck Game has the one hit kill intensity found in Samurai Gunn. The kicker is that you can’t attack if you don’t have a weapon, so the start of the match is just a rapid scrambling for firearms and panicked firing. It’s an intense, skill based shootout that I hope to be playing for the next 10 years at least.
Duck Game’s true greatness is its subtleties present in its design. At first it may seem constraining to not be able to aim in all directions like you would expect, but you eventually find that if you’re pressed up against an object your duck aims upward, still allowing you to fire. A particular gun that looks like a giant magnum recoils with each shot, letting you aim slightly higher to hit enemies, essentially you exploit a handling characteristic of the weapon into a game mechanic. The ducks can even float around on stubby wings and slide on their knees if you duck while running (ha ha), allowing you to do Matrix-like dodges against your enemies. Really great stuff, with a high skill ceiling but still easy enough to allow new players to get the drop on more experienced ones, which is the “sweet spot” I adore in competitive games. There’s a button completed dedicated to quacking (SERIOUSLY) which adds a layer of absurdity and humor to the already ridiculous setting that Duck Game takes place in.
One fear I have is the staying power of the online community. Too many indie games, have I bought on a super-sale only to see that the fan base has since moved on to other games. Duck Game is still relatively new as of 6/22/2015, so finding a game isn’t too difficult, but I really, really REALLY hope this game has longevity in the future. Like I said, 10 years please. One of the upsides this game has over Samurai Gunn is its near perfect online gameplay, which I hope keeps the game alive. I only had a couple of disconnects but the lag never really messed with me too bad. Even if the online dies out, with the local play, all it requires really is a couple of controllers and a few brewskies to have a great time. I love this game.

I have played Fallout Shelter on PC using Bethesda Launcher (without spending money) for some time and now on Steam for short amount of time (spent about 10€) and here's my thoughts.
I think some people are overreacting when it comes to Fallout Shelter in my opinion. Yes, it's free-to-play game with microtransactions, yes it's mobile game port, and yes it is sorta cash-grab game, but some people ignore the fact that you can manage without using real money to buy lunchboxes, nuka-cola quantum etc. Since this is a spin-off game, I don't mind that it doesn't have anything else to do with Fallout other than the setup, characters and equipment. It isn't a canon, so just having characters like Three-Dog in your vault is actually a bit funny and it doesn't take away from the main series.
I might be greedy capitalist for saying this, but I don't mind the microtransactions in this game. It's a free-to-play game, so Bethesda needs to get money from somewhere and thats OK in my book. You can manage your vault without spending money if you don't build too quickly and take a lot stimpaks for quests, while also saving some of them incase of accidents and raids. In fact, you can get lunchboxes and other stuff (that can be bought with real money from shop) from challenges and quests. In-app purchases mainly boosts your speed in gameplay. While it is technicaly a pay-to-win, I should mention that this isn't a multiplayer game, so it shouldn't be that bad. If there is something to complain about MT's in Fallout Shelter it's the fact that you lose every lunchbox when you lose the game. It doesn't transfer your items to other vaults even if you wanted that, so money would not be wasted. If I'm wrong on this issue, please correct me.
It's purely your choice if you want to spend your money on Fallout Shelter. Find out what they do, what you could get and are you willing to spend money on them?
But what about the game itself? I'll make this short, because I'm lazy.
GOOD:
+Art style is typical Fallout and vault dwellers' look is based on Fallout vault boys/girls
+Though limited at early stages, you can customize your vault dwellers and your vault
+Legendary characters and items from Fallout 3 and 4 (No New Vegas unfortunately :( )
+Quests and random encounters offer something to do and you usually get good rewards.
+Simple gameplay, simple fun
+Free updates that usually add something new (quests are in my opinion the best one so far) to game and aren't just bug fixes
+It's free and a good time waster. Nothing too serious
NEUTRAL:
*It's up to you if spending money on in-app purchases are worth it. They speed up the game, but it's not mandatory to survive
*Since this is a mobile game, it's about doing something for 5-10 minutes and most of the time is about waiting
*Obviously this game isn't for everyone and it might be boring to some people. Understandably so
BAD:
-At later stages, the enemies are bullet sponges and that includes radroaches too (seriously?!!!)
-Some enemies have BS abilties (like teleporting) and weird enemy spawns (raider place with mole rats at front entrance), though understandably for gameplay reasons
-While microtransactions aren't that bad, however you don't want to lose since you lose everything when it happens
-Lacks the global inventory for your bought items
If there is a better mobile game, please tell me in the comments and also let me know if I missed something important or if my review has mistakes. For now, I think this is one of the better mobile game in the market.

Full of sheep, graphics that induce LSD type trances and later, hypnotic trance music, Llamasoft games are an experience beyond just merely shooting things, you find youself zoning out and playing with your subconscious.  Gridrunner Revolution is classic Llamasoft at its best and the bonus Vic20 mode unlocked after completing the first level set (all levels named after increasingly strong curries) will take you back to your misplaced youth.
If you grew up playing Playstation or Xbox games, then there will be a huge dose of WTF and this game will probably not be for you.  Go search youtube for some gameplay videos if you are unsure.  If you want a surreal, hypnotic blaster, then this is money well spent.

Hard West is a like a burrito. The meat is a tactical, 3rd person, turn based, small-squad-combat game. The wrapper is a strategic overview that helps direct a fairly interesting and every-changing story. And the very tasty sauce is an environment that combines the old west with a bit of a badness directed by Old Scratch himself. So let's break each of those down, shall we?
The tactical combat is the core of the game. If you don't like it then this game isn't for you. It's done similarly to XCOM or other games of this ilk. There are a handful of weapons (as usual, I love being a sniper) and a couple of abilities depending on the person. The ricochet ability is one that's built into maps that can be quite fun to pull off. It's not as deep as some of the tactical shooters - it's more of a beer and pretzels type game.
There is one new wrinkle which is really interesting here which is the Luck system. Essentially, if they shoot at you and miss then you're going to lose luck and will need to move as the next shot has a better chance of hitting. If they shoot at you and get a hit, you're going to build luck. No more sitting in a well covered spot and picking off the enemy. Once they zero you in, you're going to move. Now there is a downside to this as some skills take luck. If you can't build it, you can't use those skills. But I think that's not really a big issue because if you're not building luck it means you're not getting hit anyway and are probably winning the battle. You're always well rewarded for proper planning, getting higher than your opponent and for staying in cover.
Let me address a few common complaints in many reviews. So let's talk about the RNG, the overwatch system, the AI and the save system.
1. I've experenced no issues whatever with the RNG. It's absolutely fair. 80% shots hit 80% of the time. There's nothing wrong here and the aforementioned luck system really helps level things out.
2. There's no overwatch system for you. There is for an enemy, bascially to prevent you from running right up to them during your turn and shooting them point blank. I don't find this an issue. An overwatch system would make this game pitifully easy because of the AI (point 3) and the fact you're not incredibly overmatched in tech like you are in XCOM. Different games, different needs.
3. The AI is dumb. Most battles won't be a major challenge because the AI simply doesn't do a good job of fighting. If you know how to flank then you're going to win most battles easily.
4. The biggest complaint - and the reason I didn't buy this game - was because there was no in-mission save system. This was rectified in patch 1.5 and it seems to work fine.
The maps are well drawn and usually offer a couple of different objectives. The sprites and music are fine. There's nothing particularly wrong with this portion of the game but it does get a bit repetitive due to the lack of options. The voice overs, sounds...they're all fine. Nothing outstanding but professionally done.
So that's the beef. The shell is the strategic story layer. Frankly, there's not much to this. Some well-done voice work and a few choices that don't seem to matter all that much. You click on the map to further the story and read some text. It's almost an afterthought trying to drive the tory forward and all it really does is drives the game towards the next tactical battle. The story isn't uninteresting but it's never gripping either. You simply don't spend long enough to get to know the characters you're using. Sometimes you're using a decent person. Other times you're manipulating someone who is a baddie. But it changes enough that there's never any feel for these people. It's like a story where each chapter is told from a different viewpoint. That drives the story along but it doesn't help us feel much for the characters. In fact, the story really feels a bit disjointed. I don't konw if that's the order I played these scenarios in but it's not a gripping narrative.
Finally, there's the enviornment - the Old West coupled with a bit of devilry. It's a great combo and one that should be used more. I'm not a big Old West fan but it offers a lot of atmosphere to this game that otherwise would be missing. The setting gives the story what little weight it has and it works. There is so much more potential here and I hope they make another one of these to really exploit the setting.
So, what's the verdict? I'm still playing it. It's worth what they're asking for it but by now you can get it on sale. If you have any interest in this type of combat or even just the setting then it's worth the asking price. I feel badly about paying only $5 because it's a quality product. That's a heck of a bargain. Even more importantly, it's worth my time to play it.

I was a pretty big fan of GridRunner++ after being introduced to it years ago, and it was one of those great "pick up and play" games I'd throw on every now and then for a good score-running time.
GridRunner Revolution has just never managed to hold me the way the original game has. One is supposed to derive a sense of satisfaction out of curving bullets around the screen to create a psychedelic swath of death, but I've never been able to figure out exactly how this mechanic works or if I'm actually playing it right due to the game's lack of real feedback. I have no idea why my bonus indicator hovers at 10-30 and suddenly spikes to 150+, and am never able to replicate the events that led to it. Giving the player random ships with every life, each with different firing angles and speeds, also doesn't really help one learn much either. It just feels like a big random mess that I'm somehow surviving.
Stages never really feel like they get a chance to breathe long enough and the game doesn't really seem to start until well the Vindaloo stages, which is well over half the game. The first 100 stages are just boring and slow, and the last half whizzes by because the required enemy counts to finish each stage feel too low.
I'll just remain content being at odds with critics on this one. Bummer that GridRunner++ is no longer for sale, because I'd really recommend that one over this revolution.

Chronicles was the last game to use polygonic graphics for character designs and levels as well as a follow up to Last Revelation. The fate of Lara in the last game was unclear, as in this game her friends believe that she is dead and end up recounting stories of her previous adventures. All of the game play focuses on a series of four different flashbacks, while the present day events are only shown in the FMVs. The game show cases slightly more improvements on the gameplay while the graphics are about the same. Levels are hard at times, but anyone who's played these games will know what to expect. I am a fan of origin stories so I do enjoy the concept of a game that delves into other adventures Lara had besides the adventures we already seen her in the previous games.

The Witcher 2.... Where to start? The company is offering free DLCS and long term support and also made the game no DRM. Which means there is no negative effect on performance due to protection.
The game itself has excellent story telling elements. Alongside the fact that every mission you do effects the outcome of you're stories which can result to 16 different endings makes this game have alot of replay value.
The gameplay however is a deep learning curve. Anyone who hasn't played the witcher 1 prepare for a bit of dieing. The basic idea is that you use steel sword against humans, and silver against monsters. They took a odd approach in making you need to drink potions before combat in order to use them to your advantage. I found this a very huge turn in how difficult a rpg can be. Generally in other rpgs like Skyrim for example you had the handicap of being able to pause the game and drink some HP or mana potions. In this game you need to really know what your doing and what your about to fight in trial and error to prepare well.
The game has a few mini-games that really add to the overall experience (Brawls,Gambling). The dice games and brawls have their own narrative in which you will get certain items or information you otherwise might not have obtained and has some-what importance though they are not vital to the overall experience.
The graphics are constantly compared to Crysis. While it might not have better graphics tech wise. Many agree its artistic value is far superior to that of Crysis.
Overall the witcher 2 is a great game that I would recommend anyone who is already into fantasy RPGs and is looking for another solid game to play with good story elements.

Long Version:
I don't know exactly what to say, but it's an intringuing game that, in a way, tells you how an utopistic world with no problem could behave against other worlds who have issues like ours; I can't really tell much without spoil it and all I can say, it will make you ask a lot of questions on "how" or "why" they do this and "how" or "why" did it turn like this.
As for the game itself, it's played like a Visual Novel (aka, if you want action, don't even bother play this one) and despite some issues that doesn't ruin the game (no voice acting, weird clothing, some lack of backstory or details), the game it's good enough that will make you wonder what's coming next.
The real issues, however, aren't exactly real but still bothers me:
1) the main character, despite being the "next" mediator, definitely seems careless and unless you go through some endings (which change somethings, but nothing drastic to extreme points) you don't see a lot of initiative, but a lot of complains; I can glance over the fact that she has no real ideas what's a world different from hers, but still acting completely careless or annoyed doesn't involve US. "If the main character doesn't care, how can we?"
2)The game is very short, and basically lasts 2 to 3 hours: after that you can do the endings, but they won't take so much time to unlock. The real issue here actually is that it ends pretty suddenly and, really, I don't feel satisfied: nothing has really happened at all and I'm actually curious on what's next, because all of the matter of this first episode is already "forgotten" later on. In short, a better ending would have been much more better (and luckily, our choices will matter on next episodes).
3) Some more choices.....yeah...that single choice wasn't what I was expecting for, considering the game tells you "your choices will affect the story of the game". I guess, until next episodes, we won't know how our decision affected the story.
Short Version
Do I suggest it? Yeah, if you like VN style games I highly reccommend it, especially in hopes to get the next episode someday: good VN are always welcome and I can't deny that I'm curious myself of what's going to happen next, since the story is set basically on a sort of suspension, making us wonder what's going to happen next, and perhaps we get some proper backstory and character development.
Skip it if you don't care of reading.

The director's cut is nothing short of a consolified CRPG.
Its basically what happens when a console game comes to PC, just the other way arround. Everything from the missing typewriter font to the GIGANTING FULLSCREEN INVENTORY SCREEN  just screams CONSOLE GAME.
Everytime I pick something up my entire screen gets cluttered by the loot screen now, just because the devs want to cash in on the couch potatoes. Its not disable-able. Yet the really important things weren't touched.
Picked up party members are still mostly mute mules with the occasional dice throw to run straight into the enemy instead of following your commands. The quirks are a collection of "don't even think about it", unless you like dumbing down your characters for RP-reasons. Keep in mind that the game doesen't give a thing about it. Even though the base idea of playing as a manic psychopath makes sense, there is no reaction to said quirk whatsoever.
The new character models don't look as sh*t anymore as the shock we had to live with in the original WL2, but they're still the exact same over-the-top models with only one or two actually being useable if you want to roleplay a sensible party. And yes, compared to other RPGs like Divinity Original Sin, which isn't all that pretty either, they still look like crap.
tl;dr: If you were waiting for a "completed" Wasteland 2 experience like me, you're in for a CONSOLE SCREEN SIZED SURPRISE. Stick to the original WL2 and give the Director's Cut a pass.

Pros:

Cons:
- No customizations (guns, clothing, cars, etc.) There are weapons with attached silencers and scopes as 1 weapon. Customization was the best in Mafia II.
- No garage to save your cars (but you can still call someone to drive it down to you). Mafia II has it.
- Too easy to complete missions.
- Enemy AI too easy to take out, seriously, a headshot from a pistol at a distance can kill him 100% of time without perks.
- Less variety of takedowns.
- 2010ish graphic (Doesn't bother me much but people are being butthurt about it).
- Poorly optimized.
- Not originally a PC port.
- No SLI support.
- Repetitive, almost everything gets too repeating.
- Too expensive for an unfinished game.
- Underbosses, you don't have to do much of their jobs besides going around killing bosses
- NO ACHIEVEMENTS FOR COLLECTIBLES! I spent 4 hours finding 2/3 of them. VERY DISAPPOINTED.

- Can't change districts for underbosses.

Garry's Mod is a game in which you can do everything and still have more to do. Just when you think you've done everything GMod has to offer, and you're bored of it, you find something else that keeps you entertained for hours. This game has gamemodes aplenty with amazing and cancerous communities. I thought after 2k hours, I'd burned out on GMod, and went to look for another Sandbox game. Then, I found the Icefuse MilitaryRP server. And after spending 48 hours straight on that server, I can definitely say I'm going to be here for a long time.
To put it in perspective for you - 2k hours is the equivilent of 2.7 months. No, I don't mean spread out or thats the amount of time I've owned it.
There are gamemodes in this game that provide the gameplay and fun of the following games without the outstanding graphics requirement:
Along with original and fun gamemodes like DarkRP which lets you pick a job and keep a city thriving, Guess Who where hiders hide amongst a sea of similar looking NPC's while the seekers try to guess who is human or NPC, and trouble in terrorist town where the Traitors who are randomly chosen at the beginning of each match try to secretly kill everybody without anybody knowing they are a traitor. Theres also prop hunt for anybody who used to play old MW2 servers.
And make no mistake, this isn't a trivial game where you spend a day or a week or two on every gamemode and switch so often that you never get bored. Once you find your calling, you can spend thousands of hours in one server.
TL;DR: Get the game. This is one game that contains hundreds of MMOs in it.

The Witcher 2.... Where to start? The company is offering free DLCS and long term support and also made the game no DRM. Which means there is no negative effect on performance due to protection.
The game itself has excellent story telling elements. Alongside the fact that every mission you do effects the outcome of you're stories which can result to 16 different endings makes this game have alot of replay value.
The gameplay however is a deep learning curve. Anyone who hasn't played the witcher 1 prepare for a bit of dieing. The basic idea is that you use steel sword against humans, and silver against monsters. They took a odd approach in making you need to drink potions before combat in order to use them to your advantage. I found this a very huge turn in how difficult a rpg can be. Generally in other rpgs like Skyrim for example you had the handicap of being able to pause the game and drink some HP or mana potions. In this game you need to really know what your doing and what your about to fight in trial and error to prepare well.
The game has a few mini-games that really add to the overall experience (Brawls,Gambling). The dice games and brawls have their own narrative in which you will get certain items or information you otherwise might not have obtained and has some-what importance though they are not vital to the overall experience.
The graphics are constantly compared to Crysis. While it might not have better graphics tech wise. Many agree its artistic value is far superior to that of Crysis.
Overall the witcher 2 is a great game that I would recommend anyone who is already into fantasy RPGs and is looking for another solid game to play with good story elements.

First off, know that The Witcher 2 is not a game that will hold your hand. If you're thinking about purchasing this, know that to get the most out of this game you need to be prepared to fully immerse yourself in the experience and pay attention to what is going on. This a game which deals with many adult themes such as politics, racism and sex to deliver a mature and complex game supported by rich lore and stunning visuals.
The writing and storytelling is exceptional throughout and the moral ambiguity and choices are second to none. The gameplay, in particular the combat, is an acquired taste but offers a refreshing level of depth and potential for improvisation when compared to games in a similar genre. Sound design and voice acting is also of high quality, with the environments coming to life through impressive visual and audio support and characters each sporting distinct personalities and prejudices.
It is also worth mentioning that if you have played the first Witcher game, your choices and gear will be reflected via an imported save in The Witcher 2, however the choices have limited effect and it is not necessary to play the first game to enjoy the second (however you will be at a slight disadvantage in some situations).
In my honest opinion the experience as a whole is unparalleled, and The Witcher 2 is easily the most enjoyable and immersive RPG I have played in recent memory. I would also advise reading the books by Andrezej Sapkowski as these offer an interesting insight into the protagonist's past. But back to the game, overall I would highly recommend The Witcher 2 to anyone with at least a passing interest in the RPG genre, it is the definition of a complete gaming package with spectacular production values and a lasting impression.

Hard West is a tactical turn-based game set in the Weird West (i.e. Wild West with supernatural elements). You play through a number of very loosely connected scenarios, each with their own overworld map and cast of characters. The combat is heavily inspired by the modern XCOM games, although Hard West certainly has some unique tactical elements too.
The environmental art is perhaps little dated but it fits the Weird West setting well. The character models on the other hand look rather generic and not very impressive.
The sound effects and music are pretty decent and fit the setting. The narrator voice acting is great too.
I have never been a massive fan of the two action system in the modern XCOM games and it isn't particularly enjoyable here either. The combat in Hard West is simplified even further and feels rather shallow and repetitive. The reaction shot system is a really poor replacement for overwatch and way too easy to abuse. The levels are indestructible too, which is rather annoying considering how ridiculously powerful cover is in the game.
The AI isn't particularly bright either and can often act in a pretty stupid manner. Enemies are often way too easy to pick off as long as you can flank them. The game could have really used more variety with the enemies and more interesting opponents in general.
Replacing the traditional dice rolls with the luck system is an interesting design choice. On a positive note it does make the game less reliant on RNG. The system also has some issues, however, and it's pretty annoying how your special powers are also fueled by the same luck meter.
The inventory management is rather basic and there's no real leveling system. The card system is interesting enough addition and fits the setting well. Too bad the card powers are poorly balanced and range from almost useless to ridiculously overpowered. It's also rather disappointing to lose all your cards and items after each scenario.
The overworld maps themselves range from passable to extremely annoying. Most scenarios have some unique overworld mechanics, but most of these are rather poorly developed and add little to the experience. The choices and consequences are done well enough, but again this system is lot less interesting since every new scenario wipes the slate clean.
The game isn't particularly challenging on normal. As long as you stick to cover most fights are reasonably easy. Poor choices on the overworld map can lead to rather difficult encounters, however, and there's no option to retreat even from optional encounters.
The controls themselves are passable, but the game hides a lot of important information from you. The inventory is a pain to use too and occasionally takes a long time to load.
The Weird West setting is interesting enough, even if I'm not a fan of traditional westerns. Writing is passable too, which is good a thing considering you'll be doing a lot of reading on the overworld maps. Unfortunately the story suffers quite a bit from the fact the scenarios are only very loosely connected.
Scars of Freedom contains one pretty long new scenario that's unrelated to the main game. Personally I didn't find this scenario very enjoyable and felt that it focused too much on the weakest aspects of the game. It is also much more difficult (and tedious) than anything in the base game.
The game is fairly buggy. I had a few crashes and the level scripting also had some issues.
Personally I found Hard West a rather flawed game with some enjoyable elements. It's not a bad game as such, but it could have used a lot more polish and a better combat system. I would only recommend it to people who have already played the more popular entries in the genre to death.
It took me little over 11 hours to play through the game main game on normal. Finishing the Scars of Freedom DLC scenario took me an additional 3 hours.

This game is awesome! I have tried both whitcher 1 and 2, (and I have not even completed withcer 2 yet) and I just like witcher 2 so much more already. I just find it better in every possible way. The problem is that it demands quite a powerful PC to pull off well. It looks ok without one, but if you have great PC, this game is truly impressive to experience.
Many loved the witcher 1, but I found it too repetitive and eventually quite boring, even though that game at the time of release was quite impressive in many ways. If you did not like the first game, chances are you'll still like the 2nd one anyway. It has you captured the whole time. It is the same lore and concept, but I still find the two games quite different.
The sound, music and voice acting is truly great, creating a very good atmosphere. The combat is great, but takes a little to learn, which is not a bad thing. I rather master something, than just hammering the mouse buttons. The game also has different game modes within the games. I sometimes had to sneak like the thief games, sometimes, figuring out a problem, and sometimes charge massive monsters. These aspects feel very pollished and well executed with lots of detail, making the experience truly great.
The feel is also often epic and cinematic. The game does a great job of making you feel like you are a part of an epic movie, but with real interaction, not just quick time events.
It also has a lot of depth to it, and you can customize your style of playing quite a lot even though you only work with one character. Also, this game does not make you a good or bad person, there are only choices, which I personally prefer.
I found that the menus/character sheet/options were interesting and beautiful, but also somewhat overwhelming. Too much stuff at times. You should be prepared to read quite a lot if you really want to understand the game well. But in this case, the writing is truly well done. This game takes time, and some committment to play through, so be prepared for some time-wasting. Worth it of course. This game has a great story, but is also just a part of a trilogy, so don't expect a satiesfying ending. But a great journey nevertheless.
This game is a great artistic vision and product with a purpose. This is not Skyrim, but a great novel executed in a RPG style. Don't miss it.

This game is an excellent choice for any wannabe engineers out there (I, myself just might happen to be one...). It has an excellent virtue of having a very flexible learning curve  - you can play as simple or complex a game as you like. The game, though compared to "space minecraft" by the media I would say is actually more like space lego. You build and launch rockets with often hilarious results - community slang for inexplicable spacecraft-obliterating bugs is the Kraken. Fortunately, these random glitches are often so hilarious that they are rarely irritating. The community is extremely active on the wiki, on facebook and other places, and modding is rife throughout it. In the beginning, you will destroy many, many craft, but as you gain proficiency you will learn an enormous amount about various physics concepts, whether in-game or on wikipedia researching related stuff, or on youtube, where again, the community exponentially grows. Good luck and krakreny flights to all!

There is a vibe of certain games, you will never forget. An aspect, a gameplay, a mood. Something, which will never go out of style. For example:
The Athmosphere of Deus Ex
The fast-placed action of any COD games
The gameplay of Undertale
The explosions of Just Cause.
And then, there's this game.
*Gameplay*
You walk around, and click stuff. It's not portal, or anything. Oh, and you can time-travel. Back. I won't spoi it.
Nice, simple and clean.
*Graphics, art*
The lighting is top-notch. A game, featuring photography as a
gameplay and story element, this is a must, but the guys did it...again.
The textures are a bit cartoon-ish at some places, but nice overall.
*Story*
Situation: you are a 18 y.o. girl in an art academy. Dorky, hipster and edgy.
In 15' (offical release of the game) some stufff the main heroine does may have looked like edgy, but me, picking it last summer, I see that nowadays a whole lot of girls have her aesthetics, and goals. Still, somehow it's unique, and I love it.
You, playing as Max Caulfield, loooooove photography. You even have an instant camera, so the gameplay encourages you to use it. There are parts in the game, which you can take photos,  you just have to see them.
*Music*
A game or a good movie doesn't have a good vibe without proper audio.
This is not the Hans Zimmer type, epic heroballad with chest-exploder deep's. (Interstellar, Inception)
This is not the Mick Gordon kind of apocalyptic, demonslayer, 8-string heavy metal. (DOOM)
This is the José González type of acoustic, lo-fi, minimal chill music, which perfectly captures the autumn athmosphere the game is set in. At times, the music gets intensive, and builds up tension. Or, it fades into sad, slow and melodic themes, that even I could cry on. BECAUSE IT'S PLACED WELL. You have to experience it.
(Quite literally, I have a playlist with all the music from the game.)
*Summary*
People may say the game is overrated, that it gets way to much attention. Guess what, they may be right for a reason.
The reason is, that there was no game, which could capture those feelings that this game did, create the unique athmosphere this game did. Somehow, LiS made an own genre from itself, because we have a serious absence of games like these.
Never have a game been able to create feelings, and vibe like this one did.

Currently at the time I am posting this I have played through to one of the endings. Though short this game will be released episodically, and choices made will be reflected in later episodes. I am a fan of visual novels myself and this visual novel is incredibly thought provoking. (For those that do not know a visual novel is an entirely story driven "game", where the only gameplay is the decisions you make at key points in the story. Some visual novels have winding paths with multiple endings each that play on every single choice you make, which makes you feel like you are controlling the direction of the story.) This visual novel plays on the theme of morality, what is right and what is wrong, and gets you thinking about your position in all of it. When you're thrust into such a situation what will you do, how will you react. It plays on your emotions and uses them to form the path that you are making for yourself. This is one reason I love visual novels because even if you play through it only once, and don't want to witness alternate choices, you still get the story because YOU shaped it with all of the choices YOU made. All in all with the great soundtrack and interesting story, if you like heavily or entirely driven stories in games, this is a must buy ESPECIALLY if it's on sale.

What's my opinion on Mafia 3? It's p-r-e-t-t-y different from its predecessors. Let's remember real quick what Mafia 1 and 2 were about. In those games, you were part of the classic, italian Mafia, making your way up the ranks, facing crucial decisions that may or may not lead to you being hunted by your own "family". All in all what you would expect from a game called "Mafia". Mafia 3 though, is
of that. You're not running around town as part of a mighty family, you're the hate-filled guy who wants nothing more than to destroy whatever business the local Mafia has build and finally getting to the head of the organization himself.
As you're making your way through town, you meet a bunch of people who end up being your "friends" (one of them you might even remember if you played Mafia 2), helping you cripple the Mafia's grip on the city, taking one district at a time. Those districts have leaders, and here is the REALLY good part about this game: Those leaders each have
encounters that really distinct themselves from another part of the game, a REALLY bad one, the build up towards making a leader show. In this process, you have to either interrogate a random NPC, kill a random NPC or destroy/steal stuff from random NPCs. It doesn't sound too bad, kinda what a game would make you do to "progress", maybe to gain money in order to purchase upgrades of any kind, but if those build-ups wouldn't be in the game, it would have shortened my playthrough (Hard difficulty, blind) by about 16 hours (my full playtime is 29hrs).
There's
and after you've done them for the first time, it just gets
. It's so bad that once I entered my 2nd district (there's 9 total that you have to take over), thinking "okay, let's see what new stuff this game offers!", I was debating wether or not to just quit the game and watch the ending on YouTube.
thankfully I did not quit, as the Story and the Characters of this game are
.
So what's my verdict? Buy or no buy? Well, first have some personal ratings...

I love this game. I have played most of the games in the Nancy Drew series, and this is one of my favorites. It has pretty much everything I could ask for in a ND game. The mystery was interesting, well-developed, and spooky in a fun, campy sort of way. The puzzles fit in seamlessly with the storyline and none of them were too frusterating that I felt like I needed to turn to a walkthrough. The setting was gorgeous - especially the castle which was 100% eye candy - although I wish there had been a little bit more to explore. My favorite part of the game was the characters. Each one had a unique personality and their respective storylines really developed over the course of the game.
This game was on the easier side as far as Nancy Drew games go. Also, it is much less puzzle driven than other games. You progress the storyline mostly by talking to suspects, which didn't bother me because I loved talking to the suspects. However, some people don't like to spend much time talking and would rather do puzzles, in which case this game might not be for them.
I would definitely recommend this game. It was a breeze to play and I had a blast the entire time.

Dino Horde is a sequel/successor to Orion: Dino Beatdown with was universally terrible. It is a first person horde shooter much like Killing Floor, but with dinosaurs, a between round weapon and augment store, and vehicle mechanics from a poor man's Halo. I felt a little disgusted after shooting my first weapon, which had a tinny sound effect and no recoil. Oddly enough, the recoil does come up sometimes. The guns just have this weak and unfinished feel. Dino waves are sent to you at lightning speed and most half-decent teams can wipe them out pretty quickly as they are sent in a couple packs that's easy to spray and pray at. When you're new, you might miss the opportunity to kill enemies or at least get a hit on them so you can get some assist credit. What makes the waves system even more terrible is the pacing. While you do have a variety of enemies, with some being faster than others, fighting them still often ends up being mass killing the Raptor-types, then finishing off the stragglers of larger, bullet sponge dino's and "godd**ned bats" trope pterodactyls. Killing Floor has a better variety and pacing of enemies, as the speed of different mobs are more noticible and require proper prioritizing and handling by your group depending on the map you're playing.
Ammo is all handled by an ammo pack at the weapon store, so better hope you killed/assisted enough dinos and be able to make it back to the stores far away in the base after the game told you to go to the other side of the map for an outpost. I can accept the texture, model and animation quality for a cheap indie title. I think the texture quality is pretty good in comparison to Killing floor, and the animation is perhaps finicky in some cases, but the dinosaurs generally look life-like. Sound assets are pretty terrible as guns sound weak, majority of the voice acting sounds ham-fisted and terrible, save for maybe the announcer and the female scout, and the same one or two tracks repeat through the entirety of the game - menus, gameplay and all. Vehicles are extra handy in later waves, but can be a pain to drive, and lead to you demise if you get stuck and a Triceratops rams the ride, making it explode. The land hovercraft kept wobbling on the ground and I had annoyances managing the tank.  Regardless, the game ended up feeling shallow very quickly - the fun factor wasn't there and I didn't see any reason to stay and level up.
I think the vast majority of the player base are probably younger types who got this on sale/as a gift and may not have much else to play. I'd hate to have played this before all the "improvements". There are plenty of better alternatives like Warframe, Payday series, Killing Floor, Left 4 Dead,  Mass Effecct 3, even Call of Duty Co-ops and Transformers Cybertron co-ops.
That being said, this game seem to have carved it's own niche, as there were a decent amount of active servers to join (like 20 or more), though that could be due to the recent .99 sale. That's probably telling alot about the quality and value of the game if it is going for 93% off when it's not a big Steam seasonal sale. I think kids and teens with more time and less money are willing to deal with this game (in fact, I probably would have been ok with it in my childhood), but adults like myself and most people on my friends list only have limited time and shouldn't waste it on this when there are better alternatives.
Don't buy it.The premise of Dino Horde FPS sounds cool, but you can get a similar and more entertaining as well as solid experience from Killing Floor. Once I got my opinion of the game, I only stayed longer to get my card drops....which I probably shouldn't have because they're pretty worthless.

This is an overall fantastic game that I highly recommend to anyone seeking a good story and/or challenging combat. The story is made whole with great voice acting, adult dialogue. and many hidden twists. The thing I have the highest praise for is how the authors blurred the moral compass, and without any spoilers all I can do is wish you good luck finding the high ground.
The combat is close to my favorite of any single player RPG. I'd put it under Dark Souls difficulty on Hard, but there are two higher I have yet to try. The combat is highly evasion oriented. You have a parry but it takes stamina("vigor"), spells take stamina, and swords do reduced damage the lower your stamina gets. I say swords becasue you have a steel sword for people, and a silver sword for monsters. Humans fight at a fairly set pace, monsters tend to be irratic and harder to predict.
There are 4 skill trees, basic, melee, mage, and items. You have to get most of the basic tree, but you would be pretty silly not to anyways. Melee will enhance your swords damage and effects, as well as your defense and evasion. Items increase the effectiveness of potions, oils, traps, bombs, genetic mutations, and thrown weapons. Mage will obviously enhance your spells. One thing I will suggest, you NEED some melee. You dont have to max it, but there are some fairly important ones to get, one absolute is counter attack.

I just beat this game the other day with 128 Hours played.
This game is really very good. The graphics are fantastic. The story and quests feel pretty believable (for a fantasy/medieval setting) and the characters are engaging.
One downside to the game is how the combat works with the vanilla game. I felt it was a bit clunky and annoying. Parrying seemed awkward so it resulted to me rolling around all over the place, all the time. This was remedied by installing a mod released by someone who actually worked on the game, even though it's not an "official" CD Projekt mod release. It's called Combat Rebalence and I think it is a must-have. It changes how combat works. It changes how XP works (you don't get XP from killing things, only from doing quests). It changes how your skills work. Geralt pretty much auto-parries to a point. If he is getting flurried then the parries will break.
After installing this mod I enjoyed the game much more.
The only other thing was I felt that gear was lacking in this game, outside of your two swords. I upgraded my swords fairly often but as for the rest of my gear I stayed with the blue Witcher chest piece that I'm pretty sure I started the game with, and as for gloves, pants, and boots well they were all pretty generic items I found throughout playing the game with no special stats what so ever. I guess that's the point of the upgrade system (oils, runes, mutagens). Truth be told though, I almost never used those items AT ALL. I never used a rune or a mutagen throughout my entire playthrough, and I only used oils once or twice. I hardly ever used bombs or traps either.
I was heavily invested in Signs throughout the game so I only needed to rely on those and nothing else pretty much.
Anyway if you want an awesome RPG with great characters and an engaging story with meaty combat (after installing that mod) then I would highly recommend this game.
